item.title: Herdr Notch 1.5.7
item.description:
Changed

  • Finer bins on the tokens graph. 15-minute bins over 24 h (was 1 h) and two-hour bins over 7 d (was 6 h). Session rows land at most once per five-minute tick, so with sparse sessions the graph shows spikes rather than a profile.

item.title: Herdr Notch 1.5.6
item.description:
Fixed

  • The popup's 7 d switch responds to clicks. The popup body's anchor replaced the two range segments' anchors, so neither segment was ever a hit target and the range could not be changed.

item.title: Herdr Notch 1.5.5
item.description:
Changed

  • The idle reveal counts time on the notch, not on the panel. The 2 s that brings the idle and unknown rows in is measured while the pointer rests on the notch strip itself; moving down over the rows or footer cancels a pending reveal, and coming back to the notch starts a fresh 2 s. Rows already revealed stay until the panel closes.

item.title: Herdr Notch 1.5.4
item.description:
Changed

  • Unknown-status workspaces wait for the 2 s hover too. They join the idle rows behind the N idle line rather than listing at once.

item.title: Herdr Notch 1.5.3
item.description:
Changed

  • Idle workspaces wait for a 2 s hover. The hover panel first lists only the workspaces asking for attention — blocked, done, working, unknown — with an N idle line beneath; resting on the panel for 2 s brings the idle rows in. Leaving, or clicking a row, starts the next hover from the short list again. The alert panel is unchanged.
  • Accept herdr protocol 22. herdr 0.9.0 answers with protocol 22 (the client-rendered shell and stable endpoint changes, none of which touch the fields the notch reads), and the 20–21 pin left the notch disconnected. The pin is now the range 20–22; the mismatch notice reports 22 as the version this build reads.

item.title: Herdr Notch 1.5.2
item.description:
Fixed

  • Footer profile names no longer truncate. The footer is pinned to the rows' width and SwiftUI's Grid shared it equally across the six columns, squeezing claude to cla… while padding the number columns. The label column now keeps its natural width; only the value columns absorb the surplus.

item.title: Herdr Notch 1.5.1
item.description:
The first version published by the new workflow. It carries everything listed under 1.5.0, which was tagged but never published.

Changed

  • Releases are built and published by GitHub Actions. Pushing the vX.Y.Z tag (what /release does) tests, builds, notarizes, Sparkle-signs, publishes both GitHub releases and updates the appcast on a hosted macOS runner; a manual dispatch with dry_run proves the pipeline without publishing. package-dmg.sh still runs locally as a fallback.

Fixed

  • The usage socket's accept loop owns its descriptor. stop() closed the listener from another thread, so its number could be recycled by a new socket before the loop's next accept, and a stale loop then answered the new socket's connections. Harmless for the app's single server, but it made the core tests fail on the CI runner. The loop now polls a stop flag and closes the descriptor itself; the test fake does the same.

item.title: Herdr Notch 1.4.2
item.description:
Changed

  • hdr runs its socket forwards under autossh. A dropped link — sleep, a change of network, a VPN flap — used to leave the notch pointed at a dead socket for the rest of the session with nothing to rebuild it. The forwards now reconnect on their own, as hdrm's already did, with reconnect noise redirected to ~/.config/herdr/hdr-forward.log so it stays off the herdr TUI. autossh is now required on the client.

Fixed

  • **The release build rejects an app whose @rpath dependencies do not resolve.** codesign, notarytool and stapler all succeed on a binary that dyld refuses to start, which is how v1.4.0 shipped unlaunchable; package-dmg.sh now checks before notarizing.

item.title: Herdr Notch 1.4.1
item.description:
Fixed

  • v1.4.0 could not launch. Embedding Sparkle made the binary link @rpath/Sparkle.framework/…, but the project set no LD_RUNPATH_SEARCH_PATHS, so the app shipped with no LC_RPATH at all and dyld aborted at startup ("Library not loaded … no LC_RPATH's found"). Signing, notarization and stapling all pass on such a binary, so the break was invisible until launch. The runpath is now pinned to @executable_path/../Frameworks.
